question: Should macOS discovery be allowed to save a direct WSS fingerprint captured before normal system trust validation when the user confirms out-of-band, or must the rebased PR preserve current main's system-trust-first pinning policy?
rationale: This is a security/product trust-boundary choice: code can implement either path, but automation should not decide whether manual fingerprint verification is an accepted identity model for discovered gateways.

options.title: Preserve system-trust first use
options.body: Require the rebased PR to validate normal system trust before saving first-use direct WSS pins, while keeping explicit prompts for endpoints that pass that boundary.

options.title: Approve manual fingerprint trust
options.body: Allow the PR to save captured fingerprints after user out-of-band verification, but require maintainer-approved warning copy, docs, and real macOS proof.

options.title: Pause under UX thread
options.body: Keep or close this draft in favor of the canonical macOS remote Gateway UX thread until discovery trust, diagnostics, and lifecycle policy are settled together.

recommendation.title: Preserve system-trust first use
recommendation.body: Require the rebased PR to validate normal system trust before saving first-use direct WSS pins, while keeping explicit prompts for endpoints that pass that boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checkout history points to Peter as the current-main snapshot owner, and this decision spans maintainer-level macOS trust policy rather than one contributor's patch mechanics.
